tiles.visual_brief: Merdeka 118 has a slender blue-glass shaft with diamond-shaped facets, an asymmetric crown and an exceptionally long spire. Elevated views across Kuala Lumpur or the adjacent stadium precinct reveal its recognizable silhouette. Distinguish it from the paired Petronas Towers, bulb-headed KL Tower and boxy Exchange 106.
tiles.notes: Seven verified photographs retained. Preferred: c7; daylight alternative: c1. All exceed 2400 px on the long side. Individual framing limitations are noted below.

tiles.visual_brief: Shanghai Tower is a rounded, tapering glass skyscraper whose façade twists upward into an asymmetric curved crown without a needle spire. Nearby plaza views reveal its spiral, while elevated and Bund-side views establish its scale in Lujiazui. Distinguish it from Jin Mao's tiered silhouette, the World Financial Center's trapezoidal opening and the Oriental Pearl Tower's spheres.
tiles.notes: Six verified photographs retained. Preferred: c1 for daylight or c3 for dusk. c1–c4 have 2000 px long sides. Several alternatives have obscured bases; c4 is historical and retains a crane. ArchDaily provides credits without a reuse licence; Gensler states All Rights Reserved. Publication rights are therefore not cleared for every candidate.
